Pairwise Jaccard similarity between species (native engine)

Source: R/pam_jaccard.R
pam_jaccard.Rd

Streams an occurrence source through the tiled C++ engine and computes the symmetric n_species x n_species Jaccard matrix without materialising a dense presence-absence matrix: the incidence is held in a shared bitset (O(n_species * n_units / 8) bytes) or – in geographic space when the bitset would exceed max_bitset_mb – in an O(n_species^2) co-occurrence accumulator fed by the cell-sorted pair stream.

Usage

pam_jaccard(
  env_files,
  occ = NULL,
  occ_file = NULL,
  occ_polygons = NULL,
  poly_field = NULL,
  poly_layer = NULL,
  species = NULL,
  all_touched = TRUE,
  occ_dump = NULL,
  space = c("geo", "env"),
  by = c("species", "site"),
  centered = FALSE,
  mins = NULL,
  maxs = NULL,
  nbs = c(30L, 30L),
  poly_chunk_rows = 256L,
  tile_rows = 512,
  threads = 1,
  max_bitset_mb = 1024,
  max_out_mb = 4096,
  threshold = NULL
)

Arguments

env_files

Raster paths (or a file-backed SpatRaster). For space = "geo" only the grid geometry is used; occ cells are terra cellnumbers on this grid. For space = "env" one multi-band file or D single-band files supply the environmental values.

occ, occ_file, occ_polygons, poly_field, poly_layer, species, all_touched, poly_chunk_rows

Identical to pam_env_engine.

occ_dump

Optional XPOC dump of the emitted pairs (polygon source only), reusable via occ_file.

space

"geo" (cells; default) or "env" (env bins).

by

"species" (default; J between species over the units they occupy) or "site" (J between units over the species they share — the transposed view; feasibility-limited, see above).

centered

Subtract the independence expectation (fastJaccard's center). Default FALSE.

mins, maxs, nbs

Binning range and bins per dimension; space = "env" only (same defaults as pam_env_engine).

tile_rows, threads, max_bitset_mb

Same as pam_env_engine.

max_out_mb

Feasibility cap (MB) for the dense n^2 similarity matrix handed back to R — independent of max_bitset_mb (which bounds the incidence state). Default 4096 (~22.6k entities).

threshold

When set to a value in (0, 1], the engine returns only the pairs with similarity \(\ge\)threshold as an edge list instead of the dense matrix. The join is an exact prefix-filtered similarity join (AllPairs-style): entities index only the rarest \(|A| - \lceil t_x \rceil + 1\) of their units and candidates are verified exactly, so results are identical to filtering the dense matrix — just output-sensitive. NULL (default) keeps the dense matrix.

Value

A list with jaccard (symmetric matrix — n_species x n_species for by = "species", dimnamed by species; n_units x n_units for by = "site", dimnamed by the unit id: terra cellnumber or env-bin index, both 1-based), by, species, kernel ("bitmap"/"sort"/"cooc"), space, nnz, footprint (units per species), cooc (the co-occurrence count matrix, when kernel = "cooc"), richness (species per unit, absent under "cooc"), availability (cells per env bin, space = "env" only), n_skipped and n_out_of_range. With threshold set, jaccard is replaced by edges, a data.frame(i, j, jaccard) of the \(\ge\)threshold pairs — i/j are 1-based entity indices (into species for by = "species", unit ids for by = "site").

Details

Two incidence spaces are supported. space = "geo" uses raster cells as units (species sets = occupied cells); env_files then supplies only the grid template – its values are never read. With space = "env" units are the D-dimensional environmental bins over env_files, exactly as in pam_env_engine.

Values follow fastJaccard semantics: \(J = |A \cap B| / |A \cup B|\); when a pair's union is empty the estimate falls back to the independence expectation \(E = p_a p_b / (p_a + p_b - p_a p_b)\) with \(p = |A|/U\), and centered = TRUE subtracts \(E\). Species occupying no unit yield NaN rows.

by = "site" transposes the question: the matrix is then n_units x n_units and J(i,j) measures the share of species common to units \(i\) and \(j\). This path always needs the transposed bitset (units x species) plus the dense n_units^2 output to fit max_bitset_mb — there is no co-occurrence fallback (it would require a species-sorted pair stream) — so it is meant for modest grids/binnings; an informative error is thrown otherwise.

See also

pam_env_engine (the PAM-construction backend), has_gdal

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
if (has_gdal()) {
  # Geographic range-overlap similarity from polygons:
  pam_jaccard("template.tif", occ_polygons = "ranges.gpkg",
              poly_field = "sciname")
}
} # }
